x: After 2½ miles Howard(Watford) led the field from Lindsell (Portsmouth) and Baker(Walton). Ken Miller was now 29th, John Thresher 50th, Derek Crookes 92nd and Jim Radford 107th; Trevor Hart being forced to drop back a considerable way with trouble from a shoulder ailment.
Ron Linstead continued the good work holding a six second lead over Portsmouth (Lindsell) with Poly a further 14secs in arrears, 70 yards ahead of Mitcham.

Charlie Dabbs soon showed he was back to his best form and with a well judged effort on Stage 4 he passed Blackheath, Walton, Ponders End and Polytechnic and took us up to second position with a time surpassed only by Lindsell of Portsmouth.

Bill Kerr took the next stage of 5 miles against Lindsell of Portsmouth and Roath of Walton. Although running well enough to beat the previous stage record by 14 seconds, he could make no impression on the Portsmouth runner although closing slightly on Roath.

Halton, Geoff finished second to Briault in the Sefton Brancker Trophy match between the Civil Service, Middlesex and the R.A.F In leading the Civil Service team to victory Geoff easily beat Price, Pugh, Presland, Barratt, Cooper, Ellis, Entwistle, Mellor, Lindsell and Holts.

Charlie Smart (still going very strongly at the age of 55!), Gordon Biscoe, Don Maclean (one of his off days), George Piddington and Chris Keavey completed our two teams. Our 'A' team had to give best to a strong Portsmouth team composed of Lindsell, Dave Cook, Hyman and Gough. 47 finished.

Laurie O'Hara was immediately up with the leaders and only Ellis (TVH) and Lindsell (Ports) got the better of him. Pat Newell was next to run on the first of the short circuits (3½ miles) and soon overtook the Portsmouth runner (Plumpton) but Reading and Windsor were soon upon him and Pat had to be…

…ected, and could do no better than 7th about 30 seconds behind the leaders who were North Staffs (Shelley), Portsmouth (Lindsell), Bristol (Edwards), Coventry (Kilby), Bournemouth (Stewart) and Ilford (Batchelor) in that order.…
